info.bio:
Banda originaria de Palm Spring, California. Nacida en 1989, creadores junto a su productor, del sonido Stoner Rock o Desert Rock. 

El nombre Kyuss se pronuncia "Kigh-us", y proviene de un personaje de Dungeon & Dragons, "Son Of Kyuss", que utilizarían como nombre de su primer EP llamado "Son Of Kyuss". La formación se basaba en John García (voz), Josh Homme (guitarra), Chris Cockrell (bajo) y Brant Bjork (batería). Este contendría gran parte de las canciones de su siguiente álbum, y salió únicamente en vinillo, de edición limitada. Al Parecer, por razones de Copyright, no pudieron seguir usando el nombre "Son Of Kyuss", así que se quedaron solo con Kyuss.

Tras el reemplazo de Chris Cockrell por Nick Olivieri, sale su álbum debut "Wretch" (1991), por Dali Records, un disco en el cual según la banda no captaron el real sentimiento de la música, era bastante duro y escaso en dinámica, además de irregular. Aunque los pasos que estarían por dar solo les darían mayor mérito por la gran evolución que sufriría el grupo. Si bien no fue un éxito en ventas, estos iban adquiriendo fama por sus presentaciones en directo, en los desiertos de California meridional, en las "Generator Parties", cuyo nombre se debía a la utilización de generadores de electricidad con motor a gasolina, por la falta de la misma en el medio del desierto.

Su primer gran paso lo darían gracias a la producción de Chriss Goss ("Masters of Reality"), en el álbum salido en 1992, llamado "Blues For The Red Sun". El nombre lo adquirieron por el capítulo numero cinco del astrónomo estadounidense Carl Sagan ("Blues for a Red Planet"), en el que realmente dejan muy marcado su estilo musical y se tiene un avance realmente significativo con respecto al anterior disco. Con clásicos de la banda como "Thumb", "Green Machine", "Freedom Run", "Whrite" o la descabellante "Mondo Generator" compuesta por Nick Olivieri, nombre que después utilizaría en el grupo del que forma parte actualmente. Este disco los llevaría a dar conciertos junto con Metallica en Australia en el año 1993.

Partida de Olivieri de por medio, se sube a escena otro gran bajista, Scott Reeder, y en 1994 sale su gran obra maestra que sería "Welcome To Sky Valley", con Elektra Records, esta vez producido nuevamente por Chris Goss y Kyuss. El álbum se dividiría en 3 partes, con tres canciones por parte, más el track "Fuckaround" y dura unos 52 minutos. En él sacan a relucir lo mejor de ellos, con canciones diversas y profundas, mejor producidas dejando atrás sus comienzos de banda de garage, esta vez mezclando sonidos mas psicodélicos que de costumbre. De las mejores canciones se rescatan, los singles "Gardenia" y "Demon Cleaner", además de canciones como "Supa Scoopa and Mighty Scoop", "Space Cadet" y "100 Degress. En medio de una gira, y por problemas personales, deja la banda Brant Bjork, y lo sustituye Alfredo Hernández.

En 1995 realizan "And The Circus Leaves Town", que seria el último álbum de la banda. No se retirarían de capa caída y dejan un buen ultimo suspiro. Con canciones extensas como "Spaceship Landing", que al final deja un track oculto dedicado a Kurt Cobain, llamado "Day One (To Dave & Chris)" (supongo que para Chris Novoselic y Dave Grohl). También contiene "Catamaran" que es un cover del grupo Yawning Man. Otras que dejaría el álbum son "One Inch Man", "Thee Ol' Boozeroony" y "El Rodeo".

Aunque Luego de su disolución que no fue definitiva todavía, se volverían a juntar en 1997 para un Split EP con 3 canciones de "Kyuss" y 3 Canciones de "Queens of The Stone Age", el proyecto que se traia entre manos Josh Homme y Alfredo Hernández, que luego incluiría a Nick Olivieri.Mas Tarde saldría la única recopilación de lo mejor de "Kyuss", en el año 2000, llamado "Muchas Gracias". Este contendría lo que se consideraría las mejores canciones del grupo, algunas rarezas y canciones en directo.

Una vez hecha definitiva la separación, los ya ex-miembros se embarcarían en proyectos aparte, John García en grupos como "Slo-Burn", "Hermano" y "Unida". Brant Bjork luego de dejar Kyuss se unio a "Fu Man Chu", "Che", participo en una de las "Desert Sessions" y actualmente esta en "Brant Bjork and Bros". Scott Reader tuvo participacion en "Unida", y también se presento en la audición para ser el nuevo bajista de "Metallica", actualmente forma parte de un cuarteto llamado "Butcher". Nick Olivieri, en 1998 se unió a "Queens Of The Stone Age", tambien participó en las "Desert Sessions", y actualmente esta en "Mondo Generator". Alfredo Hernández tocaría en "Yawning Man". El más productivo fue Josh Homme, quien en algunas presentaciones toco en "Screaming Trees", fundador de "Queens of The Stone Age", participante activo en todas las "Desert Sessions", estuvo de invitado en "Mark Lanegan Band",  también toca la batería en "Eagles of Death Metal" y en estos momentos forma parte del supergrupo "Them Crooked Vultures"

El 20 de diciembre John García, estuvo de invitado en un concierto de "Queens Of The Stone Age" que dieron en Los Angeles, tocando 3 canciones de Kyuss, "One Inch Man", "Hurricane" y "Supa Scoopa and Mighty Scoop". Esto dejaría una gran serie de rumores del regreso de la banda, que más tarde negaría Josh Homme.

Como dato en el año 2006 existió un disco tributo a esta gran banda llamado "Listen without distraction" hecho por bandas de Argentina. . User-contributed text is available under the Creative Commons By-SA License; additional terms may apply.

podcast.title: Dave Grohl's Discovery (1992)
podcast.body: Dave Grohl first encountered Josh Homme and Nick Oliveri in 1992 while they were performing as Kyuss, leading to a friendship that developed after the show. "Dave first saw Josh and Nic when they were still in Kaes, this would be 1992."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Secrets of Queens of the Stone Age: Part 2

podcast.title: Breakup in 1995
podcast.body: Kyuss broke up in October 1995, with the lineup consisting of Josh Homme, Scott Reeder on bass, Fredo Hernandez on drums, and John Garcia on vocals. The breakup appeared amicable, largely due to boredom and a desire by members like Josh Homme (who was 21 at the time, having started when he was 17) to explore other musical avenues. "And then suddenly, out of nowhere, in October of 1995, caes broke up. At the time, the group consisted of Josh, Scott Reader on bass, drummer Fredo Hernandez, and singer John Garcia. The breakup seemed to be fairly friendly. Everybody just seemed to be bored. It was time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Secrets of Queens of the Stone Age: Part 1

podcast.title: Anti-Radio Philosophy
podcast.body: Kyuss intentionally avoided mainstream radio appeal, actively working to write songs that would "make radio cringe." They would even cut out parts that sounded too much like a catchy chorus, focusing instead on building a cult following. "In fact, they worked hard at writing songs that would make radio cringe, except interestingly, a station in Minneapolis who became a big supporter. If something sounded too much like a catchy chorus, they'd actually cut that from the song."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Secrets of Queens of the Stone Age: Part 1

podcast.title: Calls for Reunion
podcast.body: There are ongoing requests and hopes for a Kyuss reunion, although it has not yet occurred. "And while there were still calls for Kias to reunite, that hasn't happened, at least not yet."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Secrets of Queens of the Stone Age: Part 2

podcast.title: Career Highlight
podcast.body: A notable achievement for Kyuss was opening for Metallica during their tour in Australia. "Their career highlight was opening for Metallica in Australia."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Secrets of Queens of the Stone Age: Part 1

podcast.title: Distinctive Guitar Sound
podcast.body: Kyuss developed a unique sound by tuning guitars down as low as possible, to the point where the strings were floppy. Josh Homme further enhanced this by running his guitar through both guitar and bass amps and cabinets, making the low end particularly prominent. "The guitars were tuned down as low as possible, right to the point where the strings were so floppy that they couldn't be played. The sounds that came out seemed to appeal to the stoners in the crowd, so they went with that."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Secrets of Queens of the Stone Age: Part 1

podcast.title: Lineup Instability and Label Issues
podcast.body: The band experienced numerous lineup changes, including Nick Oliveri leaving and returning, and two different drummers and bass players over time. They also faced challenges when their record label went under and they were absorbed into Elektra, a major label part of the Warner Empire, which they disliked. "And the low light was probably all the lineup changes. Nick all of a very left and came back. The band went through two drummers and two bass players. And there were other problems. Their record label went under and they got absorbed into Elektra, part of the major label Warner Empire. That didn't sit well with them."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Secrets of Queens of the Stone Age: Part 1

podcast.title: Manager Firing
podcast.body: Kyuss made the decision to fire their manager at some point in their career. "And oh, they also fired their manager."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Secrets of Queens of the Stone Age: Part 1

podcast.title: Musical Influence and Genre Pioneering
podcast.body: Kyuss was highly influential, considered "ground zero" for a new form of fuzzy guitar music. They were credited with pioneering genres known as Desert Rock, Dirt Rock, and particularly Stoner Rock, a term Josh Homme personally disliked. "They were ground zero of a new form of fuzzy guitar music. Some called it Desert Rock. You can see why. And others used the term Dirt Rock. But the one that really stuck was Stoner Rock."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Secrets of Queens of the Stone Age: Part 1

podcast.title: Name Origin and Change
podcast.body: Initially known as Sons of Kyuss, the name was derived from the Dungeons and Dragons game, where "Caes" (Kyuss) is an evil high priest with hideous offspring. The band shortened their name to just "Kyuss" in 1990 at the insistence of their record label, Dali. "Now that makes no sense unless you play Dungeons and Dragons. The game features an evil high priest called caes, and he had some hideous offspring, hence sons of caes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Secrets of Queens of the Stone Age: Part 1

podcast.title: Original Members' Collaboration with Queen of the Stone Age
podcast.body: Original members of Kyuss (inferred from "Calleos") have collaborated on Queen of the Stone Age's projects, underscoring the deep roots and connections within the rock scene, particularly given Josh Homme's past in Kyuss. "han pasado miembros originales de Calleos."

podcast.title: Pre-Queens Foundation
podcast.body: Kyuss is considered a pivotal "pre-Queens" band, representing a significant part of the early history for Josh Homme and Nick Oliveri and contributing to the "deep history" that preceded Queens of the Stone Age. "the story of Kias, the most important of all of the pre-Queen's bands"

podcast.title: Reunion of Homme and Oliveri
podcast.body: After some detours following their time in Katzenjammer, Josh Homme and Nick Oliveri reunited as bandmates in Kyuss. "After some detours, they eventually ended it back together in a band called Kias."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: You're Fired!

podcast.title: Sales and Success Metrics
podcast.body: For Kyuss, selling 40,000 copies of an album was considered a significant victory, reflecting their focus on a cult following rather than mass appeal. "And if an album sold 40,000 copies, that was fine. That was the big victory for them."

concerts.title: Metallica Australia Tour (1992)
concerts.body: Kyuss secured an opening slot for Metallica's tour of Australia in 1992, an opportunity facilitated by Dave Grohl. "A few years later, Dave managed to help get Kaes the opening slot on a Metallica tour of Australia"

srcs.episode: Secrets of Queens of the Stone Age: Part 1

xref.title: Band Naming Origin
xref.body: The name "Queens of the Stone Age" originated from producer Chris Goss, a member of Masters of Reality, who would jokingly refer to Kyuss as "Queens of the Stone Age" during studio sessions, suggesting they sounded like royal women of the Stone Age. Josh Homme found the phrase cool and funny, especially imagining it on a marquee or concert ticket, leading him to adopt it for his new project. "Whenever he was in the studio with the band, he would yell at Kias, calling them Queens of the Stone Age. As in you guys all sound like Queens of the Stone Age."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Secrets of Queens of the Stone Age: Part 1

xref.title: Early Kyuss Member
xref.body: Nick Oliveri was Josh Homme's friend and played bass on the 1987 Sons of Kyuss demo. He later left the band and then rejoined. "Josh is buddy Nick Olivary, drummer Brett Bjork and singer John Garcia, recorded a demo."

xref.title: Musical Direction Shift
xref.body: After Kyuss, Josh Homme aimed for a "clean slate" with Queens of the Stone Age, desiring a sound that was shorter, sharper, tighter, cleaner, and more focused, consciously moving away from the long stoner rock jams of his previous band. "Josh wanted a clean slate, so no more long-stone or rock jams. It said to be shorter, sharper, tighter, cleaner, and with more focus."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Secrets of Queens of the Stone Age: Part 1

xref.title: Originator of "Queens of the Stone Age" Name
xref.body: Goss coined the term "Queens of the Stone Age" as a studio nickname for Kyuss, which Josh Homme later adopted for his new band. "Whenever he was in the studio with the band, he would yell at Kias, calling them Queens of the Stone Age. As in you guys all sound like Queens of the Stone Age."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Secrets of Queens of the Stone Age: Part 1

xref.title: Post-Kyuss Career Change
xref.body: After the breakup of Kyuss, John Garcia made a significant career shift, becoming a veterinary surgeon. "But John Garcia, the singer, pulled a big left turn. He became a veterinary surgeon."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Secrets of Queens of the Stone Age: Part 1

xref.title: Post-Kyuss Musical Influences
xref.body: Following the breakup of Kyuss, Homme's musical direction was significantly influenced by his discovery of albums like Iggy Pop's "Lust for Life" and "The Idiot," steering him towards a new sound distinct from Kyuss's. "It was around this time that Josh discovered albums like Lust for Life and the Idiot. That was the kind of music he wanted to make now, not whatever Kaya's was doing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Secrets of Queens of the Stone Age: Part 1

xref.title: Screaming Trees Tour as Guitarist
xref.body: Josh Homme spent two years touring as the rhythm guitarist for the Seattle band Screaming Trees after meeting their singer Mark Lanegan, a Kyuss fan. He was described as a six-foot-five red-haired rhythm guitarist during their Lollapalooza 1996 set. "Mark was a fan of Kaya's and needed someone to tour with the trees and ask Josh if he would like to be his guitarist. So he did that for two years. If you were at Lollapalooza in 1996 and saw the tree set, that six foot five red-haired rhythm guitarist was Josh Hommie."
